subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should the shared read tool implement a compact unsupported-binary-document fallback now, or should document formats be handled only through broader extraction/provider-native file work?
rationale: Source inspection proves the token-waste path still exists, but the issue offers fallback, parser, and description-only directions, and those choices affect core behavior versus broader document/media surfaces.

options.title: Ship Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a bounded detector in the current shared read tool and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

options.title: Defer To Extraction Work
options.body: Keep this issue open as part of broader document parsing and provider-native file support, accepting that direct read can still waste tokens until that lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Change tool guidance without runtime blocking, which is lower risk but does not prevent accidental binary reads.

recommendation.title: Ship Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a bounded detector in the current shared read tool and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read-tool implementation and wrapper history make steipete the strongest owner for the shared read-tool behavior decision.
